issues.failure_explanation: Every parametrization decomposes as f = f_V + f_{V^perp}, so the statement claims that a linear encoder suffices for every manifold. This contradicts the paper's own noisy-coil example. The supporting argument (sec:lem_enc) only covers the case where f_V is invertible, i.e. M is a graph over an n-dimensional subspace V that is complementary to the encoder kernel.

issues.overall_effect: The stated class of exactly representable manifolds is wrong, and so is the main-results bullet that restates it.

issues.failure_explanation: th:uap gives uniform approximation of a given continuous map; it does not give exact injective encoding. Exact encoding requires a continuous injective Psi' from M into R^n, which can fail for n = m. For example, a circle (m = 1) admits no continuous injection into R^1. The proposition has no proof and no condition on n.

failure_location.quote: A non-linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ generic manifolds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require n large enough that M embeds in R^n (e.g. n >= 2m+1 by an embedding theorem), and distinguish existence of exact maps from their NN approximation.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that fully nonlinear autoencoders achieve zero representation error for generic manifolds at the allowed latent sizes is unsupported.
issues.title: Exact reproduction of generic manifolds claimed from an approximation theorem, without any dimension condition

diagnostic_evidence.quote: each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$
there is a ReLU neural network $N_f$

issues.failure_explanation: A layer sigma(Wx+b) with n_l >= n_{l-1} need not be injective. W can be rank-deficient, and ReLU, the activation in th:uap, is non-injective; for instance W = I, b = 0 gives ReLU(x), which is not injective. Requiring every layer to be injective is also inconsistent with the final reducing layer, whose injectivity on the reshaped manifold is the real crux and is never shown. Finally, uniform approximation (th:uap) does not give exact injectivity or zero representation error.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict to injective activations and full-rank weights and prove existence of weights making the final linear reduction injective on the image of M.
issues.overall_effect: The architectural guideline that reduction must occur only at the last layer to guarantee zero representation error is unproven, and the theorem is false as stated.
issues.title: Width condition does not ensure encoder injectivity; layer-injectivity argument and UAP use are invalid
issues.why_classification: The sufficiency claim is false, and any valid version needs a new existence argument for an injective final reduction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean, so $\{u_N(t;\mu)\}_{t\in[0,T], \mu \in \mathcal{P}}$ is a $a$-manifold
Global injectivity can be obtained by augmenting the solution set with parameters and time
compact set with non-empty interior $\mathcal{P}\subset \mathbb{R}^{a-1}$

issues.failure_explanation: Each closed patch U is homeomorphic to a ball, but nothing shows that U is a neighbourhood in the whole set. Distant (t, mu) can map to the same state, e.g. crossing trajectories for different mu, giving self-intersections where the image is not locally Euclidean, as with a figure-eight. In addition, [0,T] x P with P an arbitrary compact set is not generally a manifold, even with boundary.

failure_location.quote: the map $B_r((t^*,\mu^*)) \ni (t, \mu) \to u_N$ is injective $\forall (t^*, \mu^*) \in [0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$, with $r$ small enough

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume global injectivity of (t,mu) -> u_N and that P is a manifold with boundary (e.g. a box), and conclude that M is homeomorphic to [0,T]xP. Alternatively, obtain the dimension bound for latent_dim from covering-dimension theory.
issues.overall_effect: The a-manifold claim, the latent-dimension argument built on it, and the conclusion's claim to have proved the manifold property are unsupported.
issues.title: Local injectivity does not make the solution set a manifold
issues.why_classification: A comparable result survives under strengthened hypotheses, but the advertised local-injectivity regime is lost.

We assume that $\Psi$ and $\Psi'$ are Lipschitz continuous

issues.failure_explanation: Menger–Nöbeling gives only a topological embedding of M. The DRE framework needs a C^1 encoder on R^N with Lipschitz Jacobian and a Lipschitz decoder, so that F_n = J_{Psi'} F_N(Psi) is defined and Lipschitz. A topological embedding provides neither, so n <= 2a+1 is not established for the reduced ODE.

issues.overall_effect: The claimed latent-dimension guarantee for the DRE (main results, conclusions) is not supported under the regularity the analysis requires.
issues.title: Topological embedding bound used to justify the latent size of the differentiable reduced ODE
issues.why_classification: It needs a limited weakening or an extra regularity assumption, not new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (M_{J_{\Psi'}}L_{F_N} + M_{F_N}L_{J_{\Psi'}}) L_\Psi
Lipschitz continuity ensures that the solution of the \node\ exists and is unique
$w_n(0) = \Psi'(u_{N0} + \Delta_0) + \delta_0$

issues.failure_explanation: F_N is never assumed Lipschitz, yet L_{F_N} is used. The bounds M_{J_{Psi'}} and M_{F_N} are sups over M, but for arbitrary u_{n1}, u_{n2} in R^n the points Psi(u_n) lie off M. Hence the bound holds at most on Psi'(M). It is nonetheless used for global existence and uniqueness and for perturbed trajectories that leave Psi'(M).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume F_N is Lipschitz and take the sups over Psi(R^n), or over a neighbourhood containing all perturbed trajectories.
issues.overall_effect: Global Lipschitz continuity of F_n, and with it well-posedness and the Gronwall-based stability and convergence bounds, are not established as stated.
issues.title: Lipschitz bound for F_n uses an unassumed L_{F_N} and sups over M only, yet is applied globally

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us consider the scaled mapping $g(u_n) = K_s u_n$ with $K_s \in \mathbb{R}^+$

issues.failure_explanation: Only scalar scaling was analysed. A linear anisotropic g = D changes the constant. For example, with D = diag(1,10) and F_n(u) = (u_2, 0), the conjugated field D F_n(D^{-1}w) = (w_2/10, 0) has Lipschitz constant 1/10 instead of 1.

issues.why_classification: A one-line restriction suffices, and no other result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged.
constructing the decoder as $J_\Psi = (J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'})^{-1}J_{\Psi'}^\top$
where $\Lambda$ is a square matrix whose eigenvalues have negative real part

issues.failure_explanation: For an orthogonal projection P, the nonzero eigenvalues of P Lambda are not eigenvalues of Lambda in general. For nonsymmetric Lambda they can leave the spectrum, even into the right half-plane. Example: Lambda = [[-1,0],[10,-1]] projected onto (1,1)/sqrt2 gives the reduced eigenvalue 4 > 0. In addition, J_{Psi'}^T J_{Psi'} is N x N of rank n, hence singular, so the decoder formula is ill-defined.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to symmetric (normal) Lambda and use Cauchy interlacing; correct the pseudo-inverse to J_{Psi'}^T (J_{Psi'} J_{Psi'}^T)^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that an orthogonal-projection linear autoencoder never worsens the FE step bound, and can even destabilise, fails for general Lambda.
issues.title: Eigenvalues of the projected model operator wrongly claimed to be a subset of those of Lambda
issues.why_classification: A replacement argument is needed, and the scope narrows to symmetric Lambda.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \sum_{p=0}^P \alpha_p\left( \Psi'(u_{N}(t_{j+1-p})+\zeta_{j+1-p}) + \kappa(u_{N}(t_{j+1-p})+\zeta_{j+1-p})\right)
A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.
Using the fully data-driven training, by \Cref{th:fully_works}, we have that $\eps_{F_n} \to 0$ as $|\myw| \to \infty$ and $\Delta t_{\text{train}} \to 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting eq:diff_op_tau from the zero residual gives sum beta_p (N_{F_n} - F_n) = (1/Dt) sum alpha_p kappa(.) + (1/Dt) sum alpha_p [Psi'(u+zeta) - Psi'(u)] + tau. The kappa term is a difference quotient of kappa along the trajectory. It tends to d/dt kappa(u(t)), not to 0, as Dt_train -> 0, so sup-norm kappa -> 0 does not suffice; derivative accuracy and the order of limits matter. The result also covers only training-trajectory points, while global convergence needs a uniform sup bound on omega.

failure_location.quote: The fully data-driven is a convergent method for training $N_{F_n}$ in the sense that, under proper conditions,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require C^1-type convergence of the encoder along trajectories, e.g. kappa = o(Dt_train) or J_kappa F_N -> 0. Also assume generalisation of N_{F_n} off the training points.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence of fully data-driven training, and the claim that eps_{F_n} -> 0 used in th:global_convergence, are unproven.
issues.title: Fully data-driven convergence ignores encoder error amplified by 1/Delta t_train
issues.why_classification: A comparable statement survives with stronger approximation hypotheses and a contained argument.

8$\times$Affine 9$\times$9, PReLU

issues.failure_explanation: Q is the discretization error of the ODE with right-hand side N_{F_n}. An order-P bound requires N_{F_n} to be C^P with derivatives bounded uniformly in W, which piecewise-linear PReLU networks do not satisfy for P >= 2. diagnostic_evidence.quote: a simple strategy is to modify the loss function by adding a contribution whose minimization enforces conservation
We observe a consistent overestimation of the total concentration.

issues.failure_explanation: The term is simply the componentwise squared reconstruction error, already penalised by the reconstruction loss. It does not penalise the total-mass discrepancy |sum_k ([u]_k - [N_Psi]_k)|^2, so it does not specifically enforce conservation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term with the squared difference of component sums.
